text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

An all-women panel selecting a woman over another woman tells you essentially nothing about sex discrimination. Both finalists shared your sex, so sex can't easily explain why she was preferred over you. Panel composition alone isn't evidence of bias — it may just reflect who's senior in planning or HR locally.

Raising it would likely damage your credibility and your standing for future openings.

The real issue is the unanswered request. Chase it in writing: cite any applicable access-to-information or public-sector recruitment policy, ask for the scoring matrix and panel notes, and set a deadline. If the stated "extensive public consultation experience" doesn't match the posted criteria, *that's* your substantive concern — a process complaint, not a discrimination one.
